plan.mechanism: The reporting-gold function's explicit backfill event for the one custody source the function declares: trading days oldest-first from the source's first partition day, in invocations of at most chunk_bound_days trading days each, accounts population, a dry_run invocation before each real chunk. Not planned for cottonwood or inflection: no custody source is declared for them and no function exists for them.

notes: base_commit: HEAD of the worker worktree before the first commit (git rev-parse HEAD).

Function name: the order names irpt-reporting-gold. No function or log group of that name exists (get-function-configuration ResourceNotFound; describe-log-streams: log group does not exist). The live writer is irpt-49f-reporting-gold-lambda (lambda.tf builds the name with opal_name from the firm scope). All reads used the live name.

Writers: the activity table name was searched with the Grep tool over infra/, data/ and lib/. infra/ matches: handler.py, reporting-gold locals.tf and iam.tf, and two test files. data/ matches: account_activity_lots.py and its test file. lib/ matches: none. Test files are excluded (fake S3, no production write). The live role policy (get-role-policy) grants PutObject on five gold prefixes including the activity prefix. Principals outside that role were not enumerated.

Three firms: sources.json declares one custody source (the 49financial master). handler.py refuses any source count other than 1 (lines 222-224). locals.tf one() refuses a second firm or bucket. The live function list (lambda list-functions, read) has no reporting-gold function for cottonwood or inflection.

49financial activity_table: 4 partitions, listed with the list-objects-v2 delimiter read on the activity prefix (counts and dates only). The four days are 2026-10-07, 2026-10-08, 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-12, which matches the CTO relay.
49financial returns_table: 569 partitions, listed the same way. 569 equals the count of trading days 2024-07-08..2026-10-12 from lib/trading_calendar.py, so there is no gap.

cottonwood returns_table: 3325 partitions listed on its returns prefix (a table written by another producer; not this function). cottonwood activity_table: 0 partitions. inflection activity_table and returns_table: 0 partitions each.

cottonwood and inflection demand: null. No activity source is declared for either firm, and reading their source prefixes is outside the bounded read allowance. The figure is not sourced and is not estimated.

49financial earliest_record 2024-07-08 is the earliest date= partition of the source prefixes the producer reads (dim_balance and fact_trn, listed; the same first day in both, and the returns table starts that day too). The per-account earliest positive-value day is read by the producer from object bodies and was not measured; the source's first partition is a bound.
49financial start_day 2024-07-08 = the later of earliest_record and 2012-01-01 (the floor is applied and is not binding here).

trading_days_to_fill 565 = trading days 2024-07-08..2026-10-06 (the day before the activity table's earliest partition 2026-10-07), counted with lib/trading_calendar.py trading_days_between. The calendar answered from its hardcoded NYSE fallback (calendar_source NYSE/hardcoded-fallback-2010-2027); pandas_market_calendars is absent and the module printed a WARN.
invocations_needed 23 = ceil(565 / 25).
chunk_bound_days 25 = MAX_BACKFILL_DAYS in handler.py line 119.

observed_seconds_per_day 216.7 = the REPORT Duration of the scheduled 1-day run that computed 2026-10-12 for 7634 accounts with upload True (filter-log-events on the live log group, from 2026-09-20). Current-stage 1-day upload runs since 2026-10-09 measured 96.4, 318.1, 343.5, 389.1 and 216.7 seconds (five runs). Those runs include the lots stage. The 22 chunks of 25 days logged on 2026-10-03 ran 21 to 63 seconds each (median 37.8, 1.51 seconds a day), but no account_activity_daily line appears in their logs, so they predate the lots stage and are not the current rate.

Time estimate (derived, not measured): 565 days at 216.7 seconds a day extrapolates linearly to about 122,400 seconds, or about 34 hours serial over 23 invocations. A 25-day chunk at that linear rate is about 5,400 seconds, which is past the function timeout of 900 seconds (get-function-configuration). The lots stage is one producer call per invocation, so the linear figure may overstate; no 25-day chunk with the lots stage has run, so the true chunk wall time is not measured.

Rewrite scope: run_backfill calls the returns emit for every day of the range, then the class and lots stages. The 565-day range lies inside 569 landed returns days, so returns partitions would be overwritten, not only activity partitions.

Earlier passes: 23 backfill invocations with upload True ran on 2026-10-03 (22 chunks of 25 trading days and one of 12) over 2024-07-08..2026-10-01, which is 562 trading days. They rewrote returns; no activity line appears in them. The activity table's first log line is 2026-10-09.

Lots refusals: the lots stage refused 2026-10-07 (run logged 2026-10-09 04:16) and 2026-10-08 (run logged 2026-10-09 11:43) on the realized-lot key check (LOTS_SKIPPED). Both later landed on other runs. The refusal messages carry lot identifiers that embed account numbers; none is copied here.

Idempotence: 2026-10-08 landed 6901 activity rows (logged 2026-10-09 13:05). Dry runs of the same day logged 6904 rows on 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-13. A re-run does not reproduce the same content, so idempotent is false.

Overwrite: emit_day puts the same keys again on a re-run (account_activity_lots.py emit_day, lines 1318-1353). A backfill over landed days overwrites them. The four existing activity partitions (2026-10-07..2026-10-12) lie after the range end 2026-10-06 and are inside no chunk.

Rollback: get-bucket-versioning on the 49financial gold bucket reads Status Enabled, so prior versions of rewritten objects are kept. New objects can only be removed by a delete from an operator identity; the function role has PutObject and no delete.

Permissions (live get-role-policy of the function role): PutObject on the five gold prefixes, GetObject on six gold prefixes, ListBucket on the declared silver and gold prefixes, dynamodb:GetItem on the class table, and logs. No delete. The identity of a manual invoker was not read. The scheduler role grants lambda:InvokeFunction only (schedule.tf).

Schedule: events list-rules with prefix irpt returns one rule and none naming reporting-gold. The reporting-gold schedule is an EventBridge Scheduler schedule (schedule.tf). The comment there declares cron(41 7 ? * MON-FRI *) in America/New_York. The Scheduler read was not in the bounded allowance and was not made.

Reads outside the listed allowance, disclosed: sts get-caller-identity (identity check), lambda list-functions (to resolve the function name, names only), iam list-role-policies (policy name only). No function code, configuration beyond name, timeout and memory, or object body was read.
Client data: no account id, client id or bucket name is in this record. Counts, dates and durations only.

functions_invoked, sign_ins_made, aws_writes_made, rows_written, figures_written and vendor_requests_sent are all 0. Every AWS call was a list, a get, a describe, a filter-log-events or an identity read.
